materialized_acceptance.text: AC200-1: Implement MT-197 grounded workbench/material design while retaining all original three-WP user/model workflows and backend contracts. Photoshop/VS Code and drafts inform quality/materials without defining a copied product taxonomy.

AC200-2: All internal docked panes touch at shared edges with shared resize dividers, no internal gutters or desktop gaps. Minimum sizes, keyboard navigation, DPI/window resize and persisted layout remain coherent. Distinct external OS windows retain normal OS boundaries.

AC200-3: Use consistent shared icons, scrollbars, type, materials, readable contrast and focus/hover/selected/disabled states. Verify empty/loading/error/denied/recovery, discoverability and no clipping/overlap.

AC200-4: GUI coder A owns material-docking and Handpick interaction candidates under MT-200/201. Coder B owns Vulkan/window candidates under MT-198/199. Keep candidate roots disjoint; one actual named writer handles each shared app/lib/manifest integration hook. No coder handle or Product lease is inferred.

AC200-5: Separate workflow tester performs real user actions and multi-step tasks on the genuine app with Argus/AccessKit state and captures. Prototype alternatives/feedback remain distinct from actual behavior/runtime acceptance.

AC200-6: Implement Settings module tabs with feature subtabs OR equivalent discoverable system tree covering actual existing module/features. Preserve Engine Profiles INSIDE Settings and complete profile dispatch and original MT-196 snapshots/live authority. Prove reachability, keyboard/accessibility, typed persistence and empty/loading/error/denied/recovery states without dropping original controls.

AC200-7: Workbench/multiwindow/module clients obey the single authoritative GPU owner/broker and memory-accounting/lifecycle contracts; do not create independent device/pool/budget bypasses. Keep visual/material behavior responsive to actual pressure/recovery without widening resource/auth scope.

AC200-8: Real navigation, layout/divider/component/Settings state changes and errors emit or expose typed allowlisted mechanical diagnostic state through internal_diagnostics and the existing Palmistry event path, without project contents/secrets or a watcher copied into the GUI.
